samples.question: what are needs and wants
samples.answer: Needs are expenses you must pay to live and work, such as rent, basic groceries, utilities and commuting. Wants are the remaining expenses that are not essential, like dining out, new gadgets and holidays. The same category can contain both—for example, groceries are a need, but premium snacks are a want [S1].

samples.question: explain the envelope budgeting method
samples.answer: The envelope budgeting method sets a fixed amount for each spending category at the start of the month, treating those amounts like cash placed in separate envelopes. You track spending against each category’s limit, and when an envelope is empty you stop spending in that area or deliberately move money from another envelope. This approach helps you see exactly where your money goes and prevents overspending in categories that tend to run over. [S1] [S3]

samples.question: what is rupee cost averaging
samples.answer: Rupee cost averaging means investing a fixed amount at regular intervals so that you purchase more mutual‑fund units when prices are low and fewer when they are high. This approach smooths out market fluctuations and avoids trying to time the market [S1].

samples.question: how do I scan a bill
samples.answer: Tap “Scan bill” on the Transactions page, the Scan button next to Quick Add on the dashboard, or “Scan a bill” at the top of the Add form, then take a photo of the bill or upload a photo or PDF such as a supermarket receipt, pharmacy bill or fuel slip. The app reads the shop, date, total and items and shows them for you to check before you press Save [S1]. Lay the bill flat in good light with all four edges visible and avoid shadows or folds for the best results [S3]. If the scan fails because the paper is faded, crumpled or handwritten, try a new photo or add the transaction manually [S4].

samples.question: can I delete a category
samples.answer: Yes, you can delete a category; if it contains transactions you’ll be asked to move those transactions to another category first so nothing is lost [S1].
